title: What does the gap establish?
hook: Compare dynasty labels with dated institutional evidence.

knows: Selected accounts can describe distinct institutions and dated changes.
doesNotKnow: Han/Tang capital chronology and gaps between named dynasties

objective: Han/Tang capital chronology and gaps between named dynasties

claims.text: The Daming Palace account places the Tang complex at Chang’an, now Xi’an, dates initial construction to 634 and renovations/name changes to 662 and 670, and identifies Xuanzheng Hall as a court for conferring titles and announcing policies.

claims.text: The Luoyang report places Empress Hu’s temple commission beside Northern Wei’s imperial road and palace in 516. The later Chang’an account identifies a Tang palace court that conferred titles and announced policies, with distinct construction and naming dates. These intervening institutions prevent a Han-to-Tang label gap from meaning no government. They do not prove continuous Han–Tang rule, city abandonment or identical powers at both sites. Originals remain uncollated.
